device.name: Microphone (HD Pro Webcam C920)
device.note: Device advertises the same 48kHz x4 config in several sample formats. The first one offered is I24, which the initial build could not convert - see plan_amendments.

zero_ring_overruns.correction: Literally true - the rtrb ring never overflowed, because the worker always kept up. But the audio was lost BELOW us, at the WASAPI layer, before it ever reached our ring. A counter that can only see our own buffer cannot detect OS-level loss, so 'zero overruns' was never evidence of 'no dropped audio'. The daemon must count cpal error-callback events as a first-class statistic, not just log them.

memory_flat_within_5mb.interpretation: Growth is front-loaded: 11.4 -> 15.9 MB during the first ~45s, which is the harness's own 20s retention buffer (960000 f32 = 3.84 MB) plus allocator warmup. From t=45s to t=596s the working set is FLAT at 15.8-16.0 MB across 9.2 minutes and 25 million frames. That flatness, not the headline growth number, is the evidence there is no leak.
memory_flat_within_5mb.qa_correction: QA confirmed the shape (flat after t=20s) but noted rss_growth = peak - start measures the HARNESS's own 3.84MB retention buffer, not the daemon. The daemon's real growth over 9 minutes and 25M frames is 0.1-0.2MB. The criterion would false-fail at RETAIN_SECS=27. The PASS was correct but for a fragile reason.

no_discontinuities.what_was_actually_measured: The max sample-to-sample delta over the FIRST 20 SECONDS only, because the harness retains only that much audio. All 62 WASAPI errors occurred later, so the metric could not possibly have seen them.
no_discontinuities.method: last log sample t=596s reported 28,542,799 frames; 596s at 48kHz is 28,608,000
no_discontinuities.correction: The criterion's INTENT was 'no dropped audio over a 10-minute soak'. That intent was not met.

signal_preserved.note: 0.00516 is quiet room tone, not silence. The path was exercised but not with speech.

device_loss_recovery.reason: Requires physically unplugging the C920 mid-soak. The supervisor and ring-handoff exist and are exercised by the rebuild path, but the criterion is unproven until a human pulls the cable.
device_loss_recovery.how_to_test: Run `whisperrust --audio-check 120`, unplug the C920 at ~t=30s, watch `rebuilds` increment and `frames` resume on the Intel array within 5s.

sleep_resume.reason: Requires suspending the machine mid-soak. Same code path as device loss (silent-death watchdog), but unproven.

performance.implication: Resampling a whole utterance at finalize costs ~2ms per 5s of audio. This confirms the decision to move it OFF the real-time callback: there was never a latency reason to do it there, and doing it there is where xruns come from.

defects_found_and_fixed.title: Audio supervisor could not actually rebuild after device loss
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: rtrb's Producer is moved into the cpal callback closure and dies with the stream, so a rebuilt stream left the original Consumer attached to nothing. The first implementation contained a comment acknowledging this rather than fixing it, which would have shipped a stated pass criterion as a known-broken path.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Each rebuild allocates a fresh ring and publishes the new Consumer over a channel; the drain path adopts it. Drain stays lock-free because it runs on the worker, never the audio callback.

defects_found_and_fixed.title: Unsupported sample format I24 on the actual microphone
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: Only F32/I16/U16 were handled. The C920's first-offered config is I24, so every stream build failed. Devices advertise one rate in multiple formats, and the code was taking whichever came first.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Sample format is now ranked and chosen deliberately (F32 > I16 > I32 > I24 > U16 > U8 > I8), and I24/I32/U8/I8 conversion was added. F64 deliberately excluded - no microphone produces it and supporting it would force the whole conversion path to f64.

defects_found_and_fixed.title: start() reported a misleading error and raced the device
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: A fixed 250ms sleep then a bare 'no sample rate' message, which hid the real I24 failure underneath and made P2-02 undiagnosable.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Waits up to 5s for readiness and surfaces the supervisor's actual error string.

defects_found_and_fixed.title: The verification harness would have failed its own memory criterion
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: It retained every captured sample. A 10-minute soak at 48 kHz is ~115 MB of f32, which would have blown the 5 MB limit using the TEST's memory and reported a leak that does not exist.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Retains the first 20s for the WAV and resample check, drains the rest. A test must not be greedier than the thing it tests.

plan_amendments: PLAN 3.3 assumed 48kHz f32 capture. Reality on this hardware is 48kHz, 4 channels, I24. Downmix and format conversion are both load-bearing, not incidental.
The original pasted blueprints forced `channels: 1, sample_rate: 16000`. This hardware offers neither - confirming that plan would not have opened a stream at all.
CP-2 device-loss and sleep/resume criteria remain open and require a human.
CP-2 downgraded to CONDITIONAL. The 'no dropped audio' criterion was not met and the original report concealed it.
New requirement: cpal error-callback events must be a counted statistic, surfaced in the CP-2 summary, not merely logged.

amended.why: The original report marked no_discontinuities PASS while its own raw log recorded 62 WASAPI errors and ~1.4s of lost audio. The summary was smoother than the artifact it summarized. That is the failure mode G-1 exists to prevent, and it was self-inflicted.
